newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem denies talk of spat with Duhalde.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem denies talk of spat with Duhalde.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem added gloss Tuesday to his truce with Buenos Aires Gov. Eduardo Duhalde, declaring their friendship "indestructable" and dismissing talk of a rupture as "rubbish".

Government officials revealed on the weekend that the two Peronist strongmen met in secret last Friday in search of an end to party infighting which is disrupting campaigning for October's mid-term congressional election.

Menem said Tuesday that talk of a dispute with his running mate in the 1989 presidential election, which brought the Peronists to power, "was pure rubbish" invented by journalists and opposition politicians.
"If we get together it is because we are trying to hide a savage internal conflict within the Peronist Party," Menem said in a speech to open a highway in Buenos Aires province.
"And if we don't talk it is because of the savage internal conflict within the Peronist Party."

The October vote will set the scene for presidential elections in 1999, when Menem is blocked from running for a third term and Duhalde has made no secret of his desire to succeed him. But Menem wants to avoid spending his last two years in power as a "lame duck" president.
The Buenos Aires governor has been undermining Menem over social unrest and unemployment and in a growing scandal over controversial businessman Alfredo Yabran.
Duhalde has criticized the social side-effects of Menem's economic reforms and sided with protests against 17.3 percent unemployment, while Menem has accused the same protesters of "subversion".
